text: Why can you drive into Norway with no passport check, but get checked flying into Ireland?
Norway isn't even in the EU. Ireland is. Because Europe runs two clubs, not one. Club one, the EU.
27 countries, one shared market. Club two, Schengen.
29 countries, over 450 million people and no passport checks between them. Well,
mostly. So why is Ireland left out?
Ireland has its own travel deal with Britain, over a hundred years old.
Cyprus wants in, but it's still waiting at the door.
And Norway, Iceland, Switzerland and Liechtenstein?
On a riverboat by a tiny Luxembourg village back in 1985.
Three countries, one boat, zero passport checks.
and that's still not the strangest part. Fly from Paris to French Guiana, same
country, same euros, but it's in South America, outside Schengen. Passport please.
So the EU decides who's family. Schengen decides which doors stay open. And
Monaco? It's in neither club and you still just walk in. So next time someone
says the EU and Schengen are the same thing, just ask them.
